items: Germany is a top destination for **engineering education** due to its industrial sector, cutting edge technology and hands on learning style.
Students can choose from engineering specialties such as **mechanical, automotive, electrical, civil, computer and mechatronics engineering.**
**The main advantages include:**

Many public colleges are relatively inexpensive in terms of tuition costs.

sections.title: 7. Engineering Undergraduate Admission Process in Germany

items: The normal procedure for admission is:

sections.title: 1. Prepare a list of universities and select a engineering specialization.
2. Confirm the language and academic eligibility requirements.
3. Find out if you need Studienkolleg or direct admission.
4. Prepare language certificates and academic documents.
5. Apply through uni-assist or the university, if applicable.
6. Complete any necessary assessments or entrance exams.
7. Get an admission decision.
8. Make arrangements for housing, money and health insurance.
9. Apply for a German student visa if needed.

items: Students should start early with their preparations because it can take a long time to learn a language, check documents and complete preparatory courses.

sections.title: 8. Engineering Accreditation and Recognition in Germany

items: Students should verify that the program and university are accredited, and that the degree will satisfy their academic and career aspirations before submitting an application.
**Engineering programmes** may be accredited in accordance with the relevant German quality assurance agreements or by bodies such as **ASIIN**.
But not all programs are accredited to the same degree.
Students who intend to work in engineering professions outside of Germany should check the qualification-recognition requirements of the host countries.
Some regulated engineering positions may have additional professional requirements.

sections.title: 11. FAQs

items: Q1. Can an Indian student pursue engineering in Germany after 12th standard?

Yes. Direct admission is based on the academic credentials of the student and the rules of recognition which apply to his/her educational background. Some students may have to attend the **Studienkolleg** and pass the test.
Q2. Are engineering free in Germany?

Many **public institutions in Germany** don’t charge general tuition fees for eligible bachelor’s programs, but they do require semester payments. Private universities usually charge tuition, although some jurisdictions and institutions do not.
Q3. Is it possible to study an engineering undergraduate degree in Germany in English?
Yes, there are some **undergraduate programs in English**. Learning German opens up more opportunities, as many undergraduate engineering courses are taught in German.
Q4. How long is an engineering undergraduate degree in Germany?
The length of study depends on the university and degree format, but most programs take three to three and a half years to complete.
Q5. What is the salary in Germany after doing an undergraduate degree in engineering?
Depending on the engineering discipline, organization, region and individual qualifications, starting earnings are usually **€40,000 to €55,000 gross per year**
